system: Fleischner Society guidelines for incidentally detected pulmonary nodules on CT

inputs.label: Any Fleischner exclusion (lung cancer screening, age under 35, immunocompromised, known primary cancer)
inputs.how_stated: patient-level, usually from the clinical history or request: true when the scan is a lung cancer screening CT, the patient is under 35, is immunocompromised (e.g. transplant, chemotherapy, HIV) or has a known primary cancer; false when the history states an adult aged 35 or over with none of these. Leave it unset when the history does not say.

locator.section: Implications for Patient Care: these guidelines do not apply to patients younger than 35 years, immunocompromised patients, or patients with cancer; lung cancer screening follows the ACR Lung-RADS system

inputs.label: Nodule type
inputs.how_stated: solid; ground-glass (pure ground-glass, non-solid); or part-solid (subsolid with a solid component). For multiple nodules, the type of the most suspicious one.

inputs.label: Number of nodules
inputs.how_stated: single when one noncalcified nodule is dictated; multiple when more than one is dictated

inputs.label: Nodule diameter
inputs.how_stated: average of long and short axis, as dictated (whole nodule for part-solid; the most suspicious nodule when multiple)

locator.table: Table footnote: average of long and short axes, rounded to the nearest millimetre

inputs.label: Patient risk
inputs.how_stated: low or high clinical risk of lung cancer as stated (e.g. heavy smoking, older age, upper lobe, irregular or spiculated margins favour high)

locator.section: General Recommendations: measurements rounded to the nearest millimetre; <6 mm corresponds to a rounded 5 mm or less

outcomes.recommendation: CT at 6–12 months to confirm persistence, then CT every 2 years until 5 years.

outcomes.classification: Single part-solid nodule 6 mm or larger.
outcomes.recommendation: CT at 3–6 months to confirm persistence; if unchanged and the solid component stays <6 mm, annual CT for 5 years.
caveats: A persistent part-solid nodule with a solid component of 6 mm or more should be considered highly suspicious.

caveats: Multiple pure ground-glass nodules <6 mm are usually benign; consider 2- and 4-year follow-up in selected high-risk patients.

summary.text: Fleischner Society 2017 guidance for incidental pulmonary nodules on CT in adults aged 35 or over, revising the earlier Fleischner guidelines for solid and subsolid nodules.
Management is set by nodule type (solid, ground-glass, part-solid), single or multiple, size, and for solid nodules the patient's clinical risk.

locator.table: Fleischner Society 2017 Guidelines

summary.text: The threshold for routine follow-up of solid nodules is 6 mm; subsolid nodules are followed longer, up to 5 years.
Ranges of follow-up intervals are deliberate, leaving room for radiologist, clinician and patient preference.

definitions.text: Size is the average of the long- and short-axis diameters, measured on the same image (transverse, coronal or sagittal) showing the largest dimensions, rounded to the nearest millimetre. <6 mm means a rounded size of 5 mm or less.
Low risk is an estimated cancer risk below 5% (younger age, less smoking, smaller size, regular margins, non-upper-lobe). High risk combines the ACCP intermediate (5–65%) and high (>65%) categories.

High-risk factors include older age, heavy smoking (30 pack-years or more and quitting within the past 15 years, the NLST threshold), larger size, irregular or spiculated margins and upper lobe location.

locator.section: Tobacco and Other Inhaled Carcinogens; Risk Estimation and Risk Models

definitions.text: Subsolid nodules are ground-glass (no solid component) or part-solid. Components visible on mediastinal (soft-tissue) window settings are solid.
With multiple nodules, the most suspicious (dominant) nodule guides management; it may not be the largest. The others are monitored on follow-up.
Subsolid nodule recommendations do not depend on the customary risk categories.

pitfalls.text: Does not apply to lung cancer screening (use Lung-RADS), patients under 35, immunocompromised patients or patients with known primary cancer.

locator.section: Table note; Introduction and Implications for Patient Care (p. 2)

pitfalls.text: Volumetric thresholds (100 and 250 mm³) are given by the source but are not supported here yet; enter the average diameter.
Applies to noncalcified nodules. Benign calcification patterns or fat (e.g. hamartoma, granuloma) need no CT follow-up.
Perifissural or juxtapleural nodules with typical lymph node morphology need no follow-up, even above 6 mm; spiculation, fissure displacement or cancer history change this.
For part-solid nodules, the table size is the whole nodule; a solid component of 6 mm or more, or above 8 mm, changes management.
The table has no row for a mix of solid and subsolid nodules; the source says the most suspicious nodule guides management.
Nodules on partial chest CT (e.g. abdomen): <6 mm need no further imaging; 6–8 mm need complete chest CT at 3–12 months.

pitfalls.text: If the first scan used thick sections, a short-term thin-section follow-up may be needed before applying the table.
